sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that partitions the weight matrix along the N (output-column) dimension so that XCD k receives a base pointer offset base_ptr + k * (N/8) * K * sizeof(bf16).

verification.spec: Instrument the Chiplet-task descriptor generation (Mirage codegen) or intercept the pointer passed to each Chiplet-task at dispatch. For a GEMM with weight matrix W of shape [K, N] in bf16 and XCD index k in 0..7, assert the weight base pointer for task k equals W_base + k * (N/8) * K * sizeof(bf16). Test with N=6144 (qkv), N=24576 (gate_up).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each Chiplet-task performs the full K-dimension reduction locally on its XCD, with no cross-XCD reduction or atomics on the GEMM output.

verification.spec: Inspect the Chiplet-task GEMM implementation. Verify the reduction loop iterates over the full K dimension inside a single Chiplet-task with no cross-XCD atomic add, no split-K partial output buffer, and no cross-XCD reduction phase after Chiplet-tasks complete. Confirm no HIP atomic_add or cross-XCD synchronization appears on the GEMM output-write path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each XCD writes its N/8 output columns at a strided offset into a shared output buffer, assembling the full [M, N] result in place without a merge/reduction kernel.

verification.spec: Allocate a shared output buffer of shape [M, N] and run a device-task GEMM. Inspect the output-store code (or run with instrumentation): verify that XCD k writes to columns [k*(N/8) : (k+1)*(N/8)] of the shared output at the appropriate row offset, with no separate merge/reduction kernel invocation. Test with a small GEMM (e.g., M=8, K=128, N=64) and check the assembled output matches a reference matmul.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-GEMM per-XCD partition sizes match Table 5: qkv_proj 6 MB, o_proj 4 MB, gate_up 24 MB, down_proj 12 MB (bf16), summing to 46 MB weights per XCD per layer.

verification.spec: For Qwen3-8B (d=4096, d_ff=12288, n_kv_heads=8, head_dim=128 giving qkv output 4096+2*1024=6144), compute per-XCD weight partition sizes in bf16. Verify qkv_proj per-XCD = 4096*6144*2/8 = 6 MB, o_proj per-XCD = 4096*4096*2/8 = 4 MB, gate_up per-XCD = 4096*24576*2/8 = 24 MB, down_proj per-XCD = 12288*4096*2/8 = 12 MB. Sum = 46 MB.

sub_tasks.requirements: M-major windowed traversal within each Chiplet-task is implemented so that consecutive worker tiles advance down the M (activation-row) dimension while sharing the same weight N-tile.
Code has been implemented that enumerates output tiles within each Chiplet-task in M-major order (inner loop over m_tiles, outer loop over n_tiles), matching Figure 3(b), not N-major (Figure 3(a)).

verification.spec: Inspect the Chiplet-task GEMM traversal source. Verify the loop nest is: outer loop over n_tiles, inner loop over m_tiles (M-major, Figure 3(b)). For each fixed n index, all m indices are enumerated before advancing n. Confirm this is NOT the N-major pattern (outer m, inner n) shown in Figure 3(a).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each worker computes one output tile [m,n] fully by iterating over the K dimension of activations [m, 0:K] and weights [0:K, n] before moving to the next tile.

verification.spec: Inspect the worker tile-compute code. Verify that for a chosen output tile (m,n), the worker executes a K-reduction loop over the full K dimension accumulating into an accumulator register, and only advances to the next (m,n) tile after the K loop completes. Confirm the code does NOT partially compute multiple output tiles interleaved.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that uses a GEMM tile shape of 16x64x256 (BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x BLOCK_K) for the Composable Kernel GEMM inside each Chiplet-task.

verification.spec: Inspect the Composable Kernel GEMM template instantiation used inside each Chiplet-task. Grep for the tile-shape constants and assert BLOCK_M==16, BLOCK_N==64, BLOCK_K==256 (or equivalent CK MPerBlock/NPerBlock/KPerBlock template parameters).

sub_tasks.requirements: The implementation ensures that at any given time, all workers on the same XCD are operating on the same weight N-tile (differing only in their M-tile), so that the first worker's HBM load populates L2 for subsequent workers.

verification.spec: Instrument workers to log (xcd_id, worker_id, current_n_tile, timestamp) during one Chiplet-task GEMM. Group logs by xcd_id and timestamp bucket. For each XCD and each time bucket, assert all active workers report the same n_tile value (they may differ in m_tile). Test on gate_up GEMM at batch_size=32.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes m_tiles = ceil(B / T_M) where B is batch size and T_M is the M-dimension tile height, and uses this to size the traversal loops.

verification.spec: Call the Chiplet-task setup function for various batch sizes B in {1, 8, 16, 32, 64} with the configured T_M (BLOCK_M=16). Assert that the computed m_tiles equals ceil(B / 16), i.e., {1, 1, 1, 2, 4} respectively. Verify the traversal outer/inner loop bounds are sized using this value.

sub_tasks.requirements: The M-tile and M-split traversal variants are both implemented as selectable Chiplet-task scheduling strategies.
Code has been implemented for the M-tile variant in which all 8 XCDs process the same set of m_tiles M-tiles, with workers iterating M before N within each XCD to enable cooperative weight sharing.

verification.spec: Inspect the M-tile variant scheduling code. Verify (a) all 8 XCDs receive the same m_tile range [0, m_tiles), (b) within each XCD's traversal, the outer loop is over n_tiles and inner loop is over m_tiles so workers iterate M before N. Confirm via source review and by running with instrumentation showing all XCDs process identical m indices at the same n index.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the M-split variant in which XCD k is assigned the disjoint M-tile (k mod m_tiles), so each XCD processes a distinct batch partition.

verification.spec: Inspect the M-split variant scheduling code. Verify each XCD k is assigned M-tile index (k mod m_tiles) at task-descriptor generation time, and workers on XCD k only process output tiles with that fixed m index (iterating over N). Confirm via source and by logging (xcd_id, m_tile) tuples during execution.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the M-split variant, workers within one XCD process disjoint weight N-tiles with no cooperative weight sharing across workers on the same XCD.

verification.spec: Run the M-split variant on a GEMM at batch_size=32 with instrumentation logging (xcd_id, worker_id, n_tile) at each step. Group by xcd_id; verify that within one XCD, the set of n_tiles processed by each worker over time is disjoint from other workers on the same XCD (i.e., workers do not share weight columns).

sub_tasks.requirements: The M-tile and M-split variants can both be selected at runtime/configuration time and both produce numerically identical GEMM outputs for the same inputs (up to floating-point associativity).

verification.spec: Expose a runtime/config flag (e.g., FLEET_TRAVERSAL=m_tile|m_split). Run a GEMM with fixed random-seeded inputs (M=32, K=4096, N=6144, bf16) once under each variant. Compare outputs: assert max relative difference < 1e-2 (allowing bf16 associativity noise). Also verify both variants can be selected without recompilation.

sub_tasks.requirements: When m_tiles < 8, the M-split variant correctly handles the case where multiple XCDs share the same M-tile (k mod m_tiles collisions), still assigning disjoint weight N-tiles to each XCD.

verification.spec: Unit-test the M-split XCD-to-M-tile assignment function with m_tiles in {1,2,4} and X=8 XCDs. Verify (a) XCD k is assigned M-tile (k mod m_tiles), so multiple XCDs share the same M-tile when m_tiles<8, and (b) each XCD's assigned N-tile range is disjoint from all other XCDs (weight columns partitioned N/8 per XCD with no overlap). Also verify union of N-tile ranges covers the full N dimension.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three-tier cache-modifier policy for weight loads, activation stores, and scheduler/worker communication is implemented using CDNA3/CDNA4 scope and non-temporal bits.
Code has been implemented that issues weight-tile loads with cache-streaming modifiers (sc1=1, nt=1), so that weight lines are allocated in L2 but marked for immediate eviction under pressure.

verification.spec: Inspect the compiled GEMM kernel's assembly/IR (via clang/llvm-objdump on the compiled HSACO or ROCm inline asm source) for weight-tile global loads. Verify that global_load / buffer_load instructions targeting the weight matrix carry SC1=1 and NT=1 modifiers (cache-streaming). Grep the source for buffer_load_*_glc_slc or equivalent cache-modifier annotations on weight-load paths.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that issues activation stores (GEMM outputs, RMSNorm outputs, SiLU outputs) with non-temporal stores (NT=1) so they bypass L2 and do not evict resident weight tiles.

verification.spec: Inspect the compiled kernel's assembly/IR for stores to activation buffers (GEMM output writes, RMSNorm outputs, SiLU outputs). Verify these stores use NT=1 (non-temporal, e.g., buffer_store_*_slc or equivalent). Grep the kernel source for the store intrinsics used on the activation write paths and confirm the non-temporal flag is set.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that uses non-temporal / GPU-scope loads for cross-XCD scheduler event polling so schedulers read fresh values of the global event counter from HBM rather than a stale L2 copy.

verification.spec: Inspect scheduler polling code for the global event counter G[e]. Verify the load instruction issued when polling uses non-temporal / GPU-scope semantics (e.g., __atomic_load with __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE and 'agent' scope, or explicit sc0/sc1 flags bypassing local L2). Confirm via source grep and disassembly that the polled load is not a plain default-cached load.
verification.paper_cite: Section 4.1 (Cache modifier policy, item 3) and Section 5.2

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that uses volatile loads through the shared XCD-local L2 for intra-XCD scheduler-to-worker task-queue communication, avoiding cross-XCD coherence traffic.

verification.spec: Inspect worker code that reads its per-worker task queue entries populated by the local scheduler. Verify the read uses a volatile / device-scope (not system-scope) load resolving in local L2 (e.g., volatile pointer load or __atomic_load with 'workgroup'/'agent' scope, no buffer_wbl2 or system-scope flag). Grep source and disassembly for the intra-XCD queue-read path.
verification.paper_cite: Section 4.1 (Cache modifier policy, item 3) and Section 5.2

sub_tasks.requirements: The cache-modifier selection is exposed as configurable so it can be toggled on/off for ablation, and the default configuration used for reported Fleet results is streaming weights + NT activation stores + NT scheduler polling.

verification.spec: Verify cache-modifier selection is configurable: (a) locate a compile-time or runtime flag (e.g., macro, config field, or CLI arg) that toggles streaming weight loads, NT activation stores, and NT scheduler polling on/off, and (b) confirm the default configuration used by the Fleet end-to-end binary enables all three (streaming weights + NT activation stores + NT polling). Inspect config file/source and default kernel build.

sub_tasks.requirements: SiLU activation is fused into the gate+up Chiplet-task GEMM, eliminating the intermediate SiLU output buffer.
Code has been implemented that performs a single fused GEMM over the concatenated [W_gate; W_up] weight matrix producing gate and up projections in one Chiplet-task.

verification.spec: Instrument the Fleet FFN layer to count launched GEMM Chiplet-tasks. For a single Qwen3-8B FFN forward, verify exactly one fused GEMM Chiplet-task set (8 Chiplet-tasks, one per XCD) is issued over the concatenated [W_gate; W_up] weight matrix of shape [4096, 2*12288]. Confirm the weight tensor passed has last-dim 2*d_ff (24576) and outputs both gate and up activations from a single kernel invocation.
verification.paper_cite: Section 4.1 (Operator fusion and L2 residency); Figure 4

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies SiLU(gate) * up element-wise directly on GEMM output tiles held in registers/LDS within the gate+up Chiplet-task, before any write to global memory.

verification.spec: Inspect the fused gate+up+SiLU Chiplet-task kernel source. Verify that SiLU(gate) * up is computed on GEMM output tiles held in registers or LDS (no intermediate global-memory buffer write of the raw gate/up outputs), and that the only global store from this kernel is the final SiLU*up result.
